original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).
notes: Round 4: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true, missing_theorems=[jsp_000140_main]. Round 4 attacks both halves of the headline from two new directions. (A) NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Paths.lean (zero sorry): the QUANTITATIVE form of the counting argument. Paths c = the total number of two-edge paths over all colour classes of c; two_mul_classIn_le_add is the refined per-colour lemma 2*|E_i| <= n + p (the classical 3*|E_i| <= 2n discards p); mul_n_sub_one_le is the identity n*(n-1) <= n*k + Paths c, i.e. k >= (n-1) - Paths c/n; three_mul_paths_le gives 3*Paths c <= n*k and classical_lower_bound' re-derives 3(n-1) <= 4k from the identity (so the new framework subsumes the classical one); five_sixth_of_paths is THE 5/6 CRITERION: Paths c <= n(n-1)/6 (at least two thirds of the edges in single-edge components) => 5*(n-1) <= 6*k, i.e. f(n,4,5) >= 5n/6 - 5/6; EG_ge_five_sixth_of_paths(+_real) and five_sixth_of_no_paths are the corresponding forms for EG n and for matchings-only colourings. The lower half of the catalog answer is thus reduced to ONE concrete hypothesis on the number of two-edge paths. (B) NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Ghost.lean (zero sorry): a SECOND construction, the ghost-vertex colouring c({a,b}) = a+b for base vertices a,b < m and c({inf,a}) = 2a, of K_{m+1} with m colours, for odd m with 3 not dividing m. A K_4 containing the ghost vertex spans 2x, 2y, 2z, x+y, x+z, y+z; the only possible coincidences are the three cross equalities, and two of them give 3x = 3y hence x = y because 3 is a unit in ZMod m (three_mul_inj, via ZMod.isUnit_prime_of_not_dvd) - the exact analogue of two_mul_inj for the sum colouring. The structural ingredients are properness in all three forms (ghostCol_ne_last, ghostCol_ne_first, ghostCol_last_ne), the two collision lemmas collision_12/13/23 and cross_12/13/23, the classification of the possible coincidences (mem_B_base_ab/ac/ad, mem_B_last) and the counting of the two triples of colours (ghost_four_base, ghost_four_last). MAIN RESULT: admissible_ghost - the ghost colouring of K_{m+1} with m colours is admissible for every odd m with 3 not dividing m; EG_le_ghost - f(m+1,4,5) <= m, i.e. f(n,4,5) <= n-1 for n = 0, 2 (mod 6), which improves round 3's f <= n+1 for two thirds of the even n. Consequences in Main.lean: EG_le_ghost_sub, EG_le_sixth_residue(+_real) (f(n,4,5) <= n for every n != 4 mod 6), fiveSixthUpper_sixth_residue and fiveSixthUpper_sixth_ge (THE UPPER HALF OF THE HEADLINE AT THE SHARP VALUE eps = 1/6 for all n != 4 mod 6; round 3 had it only for odd n), fiveSixthShape_sixth_residue (5n/6 - (n/12+3/4) <= f <= 5n/6 + n/6, the upper side without the additive constant), fiveSixth_quarter / fiveSixth_ge_quarter_ge (|f - 5n/6| <= eps*n for eps >= 1/4 and n >= 5, n != 4 mod 6) and admissibleLower_five_sixth_of_paths (the 5/6 criterion in the Admissible-colouring language of the reduction theorem). Still missing for jsp_000140_main: (i) the BCDP22 construction with 5n/6 + o(n) colours - with k = 5n/6 every colour class must be a spanning disjoint union of n/5 single edges and n/5 two-edge paths, a genuinely new mechanism, and neither sumCol nor ghostCol can be post-processed further; (ii) the BCDP22 lower bound, now isolated as Paths c <= n(n-1)/6. The remaining residue class n = 4 mod 6 still only has f(n,4,5) <= n+1 (the ghost construction is provably not admissible when 3 | m: the K_4 {inf, 0, m/3, 2m/3} spans three colours).
